details:
Summary or TL;DR: Use the VRC+ money to fund a bounty board system for highly requested features in the community. These "bounties" will be submitted via code snippets/repos using official means (i.e. VRCSDK/Unity). If these submissions are accepted, then there is a reward/incentive for the submitter and the implementation will be taken care of in a timely manner with an estimated time of release.
Working Example Part 1: Hackers in good faith. The US Justice Department just made it possible for them to contribute to entities via submissions of exploits as a way of providing a means of helping the entity with their product without facing prison time. This makes it easier for hacking incentives like the Google article below, but with more protection towards the hackers of good faith going forward.
Source (US Justice Department): https://www.theverge.com/2022/5/19/23130910/justice-department-cfaa-hacking-law-guideline-limits-security-research
Source (Hacking Incentive): https://www.cnet.com/tech/mobile/googles-android-bug-bounty-program-will-now-pay-out-1-5-million/
Working Example Part 2: Unitystation is a modern, yet faithful successor to Space Station 13. This is an open-source game under the AGPL v3. For development of this game on top of official means, they actually have a bounty board based on their Patreon earnings to fund bounties of certain features that need to be developed faster than the official team is able to. Since this is all open-source, check out both their GitHub and Discord for the full breakdown of this bounty-driven development.
NOTE: Recent bounties have the reward amount denoted as "B:##" in USD. 
Source (Unitystation Bounties via GitHub): https://github.com/unitystation/unitystation/issues?q=label%3ABounty
Source (Unitystation Discord): https://discord.gg/tFcTpBp
To combine the two examples together into my summary above, I will re-propose my summary, but with more detail.
Summary clarification and requirements: Using the Unitystation development model of incentivizing development via outsourcing, this would allow features to be developed more quickly without having to wait 3+ years for a certain feature. Many of these requested features are based on existing code-snippets/repos the community took upon themselves to make while waiting "years" for an official version to be implemented. These submissions could be reviewed by the dev team, then brought in-house if approved. ToS would have to be altered to protect the submitter from legal action in case if the submission was rejected and is based on existing non-malicious code. This ties in with the "hackers of good faith" example. If these changes were implemented, not only we would have more innovation, but we would bring in more help for a much better experience in a more timely manner. 
Speaking of timely manner, the feedback timeline from the VRC team for submissions need to be outlined inside the bounty. For example, for smaller fixes/features, this could be a few days while bigger ones could take upwards of one week. Resubmissions should be allowed as well, but on a first-come, first-serve basis. Instead of assigning a submitter for a bounty, we would have an open forum explaining why certain submissions didn't meet the expectations of the bounty and then reflect those expectations as clarification on the bounty itself via EDITs in the initial post. 
Finally, whenever the bounty has been rewarded, there needs to be a release date for the fix/feature in "yyyy/MM" format. Not only this will add the transparency we desperately need, but it also holds accountability of the dev team. Remember, this is using VRC+ funds. So the people affected by any deadline changes would ultimately be the VRC+ users.
Reward price point: Obviously, this would be under VRC team's discretion, but it would be depend on the size of the feature. You can see in the "bounty board" for Unitystation, there are various sizes in rewards depending on how large the feature/fix is. Depending on the income of VRC+ would determine how much they can afford to reward submitters. These reward amounts could be anywhere from low double-digits to low triple-digit dollar amounts (set in USD, then converted if necessary).
title: VRC Feature Bounty Board
